prompt:
Add an optional rendering lifecycle observer to Jinja so applications can trace template executions without monkeypatching Template methods or changing generated output. Complete the integration across ordinary, asynchronous, streaming, module, native-value, cached and sandboxed templates.

Public API: Environment, Environment.overlay and the direct Template constructor accept a new keyword-only render_observer argument. An observer is None or a synchronous callable receiving one RenderEvent; reject other configuration values with TypeError mentioning render_observer. Environment.render_observer is a writable runtime attribute. Environment construction and direct Template construction default to None; overlay inherits the existing observer when the argument is omitted, accepts a replacement, and explicitly passing None disables it. Existing positional parameters remain compatible. Callable objects, including unhashable ones, must work for direct Template construction without changing any other environment's observer.

Export an immutable RenderEvent from jinja2. Every event has kind, operation, template and error attributes. kind is one of start, success, error, close. operation is the public method being observed: render, render_async, generate, generate_async, make_module, or make_module_async. template is the exact Template instance receiving that call; error is the original BaseException object for an error event and None otherwise. Each call captures its observer when execution starts and uses that callable for the entire lifecycle, even if the environment attribute changes during the call. Callback return values are ignored. Callback failures propagate unchanged and are never recursively reported back to the observer.

For each observed operation, emit start before executing template code, followed by exactly one terminal event: success after ordinary completion, error when the operation raises, or close when a started generator is explicitly closed before normal exhaustion. Failures preparing render arguments and attempts to use async rendering on a synchronous environment are also operation errors. Preserve the original rendering exception object, template traceback information and BaseException behavior, including async cancellation. If the observer itself raises while receiving an error, propagate that observer error without invoking it again. An observer failure on start must prevent template execution.

Streaming remains lazy: creating an iterator or TemplateStream emits nothing; first iteration starts the lifecycle. Closing a never-started iterator emits nothing. Closing a partially consumed sync or async generator emits one close event with error=None and closes its underlying rendering generator; repeated close does not emit another event. Exhaustion emits success, and a later close does not change that outcome. Template.stream and buffered TemplateStream consumption use the generate lifecycle. Do not buffer a synchronous rendering generator to implement observation.

Observe the six public methods throughout the Template hierarchy, including NativeTemplate's render overrides, Sandbox environments and direct Template instances. Preserve output values and types, escaping, globals, imports, macro/module exports, extension behavior and all existing defaults. Environment overlays, loader caches, bytecode caches and templates compiled before the observer is changed must use the correct observer at invocation time. Merely loading or compiling a template does not render it. Reading an already cached Template.module does not start a new rendering lifecycle. Imports may call make_module when a module is actually constructed. Includes and inheritance inside an existing render do not synthesize extra public-method calls.

When a public sync render/generate method internally delegates to async execution, emit only the outer public operation's lifecycle, not a duplicate lifecycle for the implementation helper. In contrast, an application explicitly calling another template's public rendering method from a template function is a distinct nested operation and must be observed. Concurrent async renders, interleaved generators and reentrant application rendering must keep their observer and template identities independent; do not use a process-global suppression flag.

Add focused regression tests in the relevant existing API, async, native, import/module, loader/cache, sandbox and debug test modules, plus integration coverage for nesting, lazy and buffered streams, cancellation, changing observers and callback failures. Document the public event API, configuration/overlay precedence and a runnable tracing example; describe generator lifetime and observer-error behavior. Preserve the supported Python versions and current typing/style conventions. Run the full repository test suite and the available formatting and typing checks, fixing regressions caused by this feature. Finish with a concise implementation and verification report. Make routine design choices autonomously.
